text.p: Transport, logistics and security group Brambles Industries Ltd said on Friday it saw further earnings improvement in the 1996/97 financial year provided there was no further deterioration in either the Australian or European economies.

"Despite uncertainty in the direction of the Australian and European economies in particular, the company should deliver further profit growth this year," Brambles chief executive, John Fletcher, said in a statement.

Brambles earlier said its net profit for the year to June 30 rose 120.2 percent to A$215.1 million. The company raised its final dividend to 35 cents a share from 33 cents a share in the previous corresponding period.
Fletcher said the group's strong performance reflected the successful rationalisation of its wholly-owned businesses and continued strong growth from its Chep pallet joint venture.
Chep is 50 percent owned by Brambles and 50 percent by U.K. industrial group GKN Plc.

"Overseas profits grew at twice the rate in Australia and this trend is likely to continue. In particular, we expect further significant contributions from Chep in Europe and North America," Fletcher said.
Fletcher said while Brambles may sell one or two of its non-core offshore operations, its key emphasis was now on growth in Europe, the United States and Asia.
The company would continue to pursue new opportunities in Australia, including airport privitisations, Fletcher said.
"The continuing growth expected in overseas earnings meant that the company would need to reduce moderately the level of franking of dividends declared on 1996/97 earnings," he said.
Brambles said its Australian operations were effected by subdued economic activity for much of the period resulting in depressed volumes and pressures on margins and prices.

"However, Australian earnings were still up 7.9 percent on the previous period as a consequence of substantial investment over the past three years into expanding the contract services base," Brambles said.
Brambles said the major economies in which it operated in Europe remained subdued with the German economy in particular showing lower growth than expected.
The company said its U.S. operations were focused on the Chep joint venture which achieved good profit growth in 1995/96.

"Economic conditions in the United States continued to be reasonably favourable for Brambles' operations during 1995/96, although there was some sign of a slowing towards the end of the period," Brambles said.
At 2.45 p.m. (0445 GMT), Brambles shares were a cent firmer at A$18.86. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
